title: Replication
subtitle: Copies keep data alive and reads fast, but the speed of keeping them in step decides what a crash loses
motto: Keep more than one copy, and know how far behind each one is
keyInsight: Asynchronous replication is fast but loses the writes still in flight when the primary fails; synchronous replication loses none but makes every write wait.

decisions.title: Show data loss as the failure
decisions.description: The failure frame spikes the lag and then fails the primary, so the cost of asynchronous replication appears as a count of lost writes.
decisions.alternatives: Showing only the read-scaling benefit would leave out what a failover can cost.

decisions.title: Put write latency next to writes lost
decisions.description: The last frame shows that zero lost writes is paid for in write latency, with both numbers in the same frame.
decisions.alternatives: Presenting synchronous replication as simply safer would hide that one slow replica stalls every write.
